source.title: Sparrow: Data-Efficient Video-LLM with Text-to-Image Augmentation
source.authors: Shukang Yin; Chaoyou Fu; Sirui Zhao; Chunjiang Ge; Yan Yang; Yuhan Dai; Yongdong Luo; Tong Xu; Caifeng Shan; Enhong Chen

page_placements.theme: Fine-tuning data and task diversity have diminishing, conditional returns

record.file_problem: The paper text is present in full. Some figure labels and plotted values are garbled by OCR; the main text and tables are readable.
record.tranche_reason: It reports data-scaling results for video-LLM fine-tuning, an extension to a video-model training setting. The outcomes are benchmark accuracy, not held-out pretraining loss or fitted power-law exponents.
record.gate_note: The paper evaluates video-understanding benchmark accuracy after fine-tuning with different data volumes and compositions. It does not measure held-out cross-entropy loss, parameter- or compute-scaling laws, extrapolation from small runs, or compute-optimal allocation. Figure-only curve values that the text does not quantify are not transcribed as individual numerical results.
record.test_reason: The paper cites the scaling law as motivation and proposes a data-augmentation method (Sparrow) for video-LLM fine-tuning. Its results are benchmark accuracies after varying fine-tuning sample counts (30K–200K) on two fixed-size image-LLMs. It has no held-out loss, no parameter or compute scaling, no power-law fits, no extrapolation and no prediction of downstream scores from scale or loss. Most rows compare the authors' method with baselines or data mixes. The one scaling observation, early saturation of accuracy with more fine-tuning data, is a related but different construct and is recorded under fits_no_version.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors find early saturation when scaling video fine-tuning data, which they attribute to limited instruction diversity. Their Sparrow augmentation (text rendered as video-like image sequences) improves data efficiency: 30K hybrid samples match or beat 200K video samples on Video-MME (56.7 vs 56.3). It also improves long-video benchmarks without long-video training.
record.recipe_differences: The study scales video fine-tuning data and evaluates benchmark accuracy, rather than measuring held-out pretraining loss across parameter, token, or compute scales. It does not fit power laws or optimize a compute budget.
record.method_sensitivity: The authors report that performance depends on training-data composition: different video datasets and mixes produce different scores, and synthetic data performs better than an otherwise similar pure-text mix. Video-only scaling is described as reaching an early plateau.

fits_no_version.finding: Fine-tuning a fixed image-LLM on more video data raises video-benchmark accuracy with fast saturation. For InternVL-4B on Video-MME, 30K mixed samples give +3.1 and 100K only another +0.5, which the authors call 'resembling a logarithmic growth'. For the MiniCPM-8B video-only baseline, 60K gives +3.1 and 100K only +0.9 more. The authors attribute this to low instruction diversity, and say hybrid data scales more steadily.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Benchmark accuracy of video-LLMs saturates early with fine-tuning data volume, and the saturation depends on instruction diversity of the data.

record.problems: The scaling outcomes are downstream benchmark accuracies rather than held-out loss; there are no fitted scaling exponents or predictive tests. No error bars or uncertainty estimates are reported. Several scaling curves are only shown in figures whose plotted values are not readable in the supplied text.
record.rows_left_out: The complete numerical series in Figures 3 and 7 is not separately extracted because the OCR does not provide reliable point values. Table 3's individual benchmark rows and the text-quantified Figure 3 results are retained.

untested.parts: All: no held-out pretraining loss, and no parameter, token or compute scaling.
All: no fits and no extrapolation to larger runs.
All: no architecture-shape comparisons at fixed parameter count.
Video fine-tuning setting, but no loss measured and no power-law form fitted or compared.
Model size is fixed per series and pretraining loss is not reported. Only fine-tuning sample count varies, with no predictive fit.
No fitted exponents or fitting choices; departures from a power law are not analysed with any fit.

record.verdict_notes: This is a method paper on data-efficient video-LLM fine-tuning. 'Scaling law' appears only as motivation. The reader's V6 'supports' label rested on the authors' method beating baselines, which is method performance, not downstream predictability with scale, so all labels are removed. Corrected values: r20 should be 45.1, and r32's baseline should be 45.1.

versions.untested_parts: Held-out pretraining loss as a function of parameters, tokens, or compute; power-law fits and their range.
Prediction of much larger runs from power laws fitted on smaller runs.
Compute-optimal parameter and token allocation and its scaling with compute.
Effects of depth, width, and other architecture details at a fixed parameter count.
The study uses video models and fine-tuning, but does not test whether the same power-law form holds: it reports benchmark accuracy rather than held-out loss and does not fit or compare power laws.
It reports video-benchmark accuracy after data scaling, but does not test performance prediction from pretraining loss or report a predictive fit.
Fitting choices, fitted exponents, compute-optimal splits, and departures from fitted single power laws.

relation.reason: The study uses the general scaling premise to motivate data-efficient training, but its accuracy comparisons do not test the specified claim versions.

tranche.reason: Scaling motivates the augmentation method. The experiments compare fine-tuning sample budgets and benchmark accuracy without testing a power-law form, extrapolation, compute-optimal allocation or downstream predictive law.

source_check.notes: Section 4.3.1 explicitly reports +3.1, although Table 2 displays 52.5 for zero-shot and 55.7 for 30K mixed training. The supplied study text is arXiv v5, dated 22 July 2025.

statements.correction: InternVL; ShareGemini and Video-ChatGPT mixed 1:1; Video-MME overall accuracy; 30K: +3.1 points over zero-shot; 100K: another +0.5 points; limited instruction diversity: proposed explanation for early saturation.
statements.problem: The gains and model match Section 4.3.1, but definite dependence on instruction diversity overstates the authors' proposed explanation. Rows r13, r17 and r21 concern MiniCPM long-video results.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Video-MME and long-video benchmark settings with hybrid fine-tuning data
reader_labels.reason: The reported downstream accuracies improve over the same-size video-only baseline in most tabled comparisons, including the overall scores at 30K, 60K, and 100K (r25-r36).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Scaling video-only data, and benchmark-specific hybrid results
reader_labels.reason: The authors report early saturation for video-only scaling; hybrid Video-MMEL accuracy is unchanged at 60K versus its video-only comparison, and hybrid LongVideoBench accuracy falls from 60K to 100K (r14, r29, r34).
